mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified tightening phase.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor market participation or rising wage growth reduces risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite UNRATE increase (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (industrial production) surprises exceed +2% above the prior month's trend, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive, reflecting optimism about near-term demand recovery.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly surprise > +2% above prior month's average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat when demand surprise is positive (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% signals supply-side weakness, predicting a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during INDPRO declines of ≥3%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL by more than 0.5 percentage points indicate persistent monetary tightening, leading to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both decline >0.5pp in the same month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite the two-month dual decline (IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (employment) by over 50,000 in a month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates stabilization in labor markets.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the job loss episode.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (GDP) growth exceeds +5% unexpectedly, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive due to optimism about robust economic momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the GDP surprise (IC < -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-month decline in RSAFS (retail sales) below trend predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand erodes earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1) during the 4-month decline.
